checked: overfitting / data-mining bias (free_t deflation per cell, seed sensitivity, 60/40 out-of-sample, disjoint-slice replication)
insufficient sample size (floor-free census at floors 1/5/10/20/30/50)
unrealistic fills (fill model read directly: entry at next open with adverse slippage, stop wins ties, gaps honoured)
understated costs and slippage (target/time/session legs charged 0.5/1.0/2.0 extra ticks analytically)
look-ahead bias and repainting (prefix-stability: truncate the series and require bit-identical trades before the cut)
survivorship bias (single continuous front-month series per symbol; no cross-sectional selection is performed)
future-data leakage (contract specs verified; dollar P&L reconstructed from leg prices x point value for every trade)
placebo control (worker 1's placebo.py; three kinds, ranked in the same table)
not_checked: roll/continuation methodology of the supplied CSVs - the series are taken as given and a bad splice would show up as a phantom gap trade
intrabar order of stop and target beyond the engine's pessimistic rule
live liquidity in the micro grains: MZC/MZS/MZW 60m bars routinely show single-digit volume, so real fills would be worse than modelled

placebo_verdict.how_to_read: With k placebos among N rows and no edge anywhere, E[best placebo rank] = (N+1)/(k+1). A placebo at rank 1 in a 4-row table is not news; a placebo at rank 1 in a 100-row table with 10 placebos is.

tradeability.note: Median 60m bar volume in the micro grains is 11-17 contracts with a 10th percentile of 1-2 and 163-173 zero-volume bars in the 274-day window. The engine's 0.5-tick entry / 1.5-tick stop slippage is not a defensible fill assumption at that volume, and it is adverse in one direction only, which is the D35 failure mode: no amount of resampling will reveal it.

series_quality.note: D-worker3-1: the micro-grain 60m/240m series contain bars that are inconsistent with a single contract month. Adjacent hourly bars oscillate by ~16 cents on corn - the size of a CBOT calendar spread - frequently on ZERO volume and with high==low (a single print), and the move reverses on the following bar. The engine honours gaps at the open, so a stop sitting inside one of these excursions is filled at a price that was never tradeable. NQ and ES show no 2% gaps at all. This is a DATA defect, not a strategy result, and it contaminates every micro-grain statistic in this report on the loss side.

roll_gap_scan.note: Close-to-open gaps in the supplied continuous series. A badly spliced roll shows up as an isolated multi-percent gap that the engine will honour as a real fill. Nothing here is conclusive - the roll methodology of the CSVs was NOT audited - but a series with no multi-percent gaps is unlikely to contain a raw price-level splice.

fill_model_audit.note: D35 check. Entries fill at the NEXT bar's OPEN plus adverse slippage, never at a bar extreme, so the D35 construction (a limit filling at an extreme and then being credited with that same bar's opposite extreme) cannot arise here. The engine also resolves stop-and-target-in-one-bar in favour of the stop and fills gaps at the open. The residual optimism is that TARGET, TIME and SESSION_CLOSE legs fill with zero slippage - quantified in exit_slippage_stress.

stop_fill_quality.note: Realised R on STOP exits. A perfect stop fill is -1R minus fees. Values far below that are gaps through the stop, which the engine fills at the bar open. The micro grains gap through their stops far more often than the index complex, which is a direct consequence of single-digit bar volume and a 0.125-cent tick on a $5 point.

rth_only_arm_D24.coverage: 9 of 20 planned D24 cells completed; the remaining 60m cells were stopped for time. Paired design: identical generated rule sets over identical bars, rth_only flipped, sign test on the per-rule-set expectancy delta. No pooling across cells.

deflation.rule: free_t(screened) = sqrt(2 ln screened); nothing is evidence below it
